rebuttal_or_critique: While I acknowledge the arguments of Dr. Goyal and Prof. Varma regarding the moderation of core inflation to 3.10%, I remain concerned that shifting to a neutral stance prematurely could be misconstrued as a signal that the MPC is lowering its guard against inflation. With food inflation at 8.69% and a positive output gap of 0.40%, the risk of inflation expectations becoming unanchored remains elevated. Monetary policy must remain focused on the 4.00% target; easing now, when headline inflation is still 4.75%, risks creating a persistent upward drift in expectations that would necessitate a much higher terminal rate later. We must prioritize the credibility of our inflation-targeting framework over short-term growth considerations, especially when the economy is demonstrating resilience with 6.80% GVA growth.
